text.p: Manufacturer National Consolidated Ltd said on Friday that it looked forward to a recovery in the Australian housing sector but was concerned by reports that the government might further reduce tariffs on the automotive sector.

The company, which has Malaysian Mining Corp Bhd as its largest shareholder with a 48.5 percent stake, has operations in the local building and construction sector as well as the automotive and general engineering industries.

In an accompanying table it said it suffered a net loss of A$4.0 million in calendar 1996 after including an abnormal item of A$16.4 million which was mainly due to restructuring costs for the Ajax Fasteners unit.
The company, which has moved its financial year-end to December from June, earned A$11.4 million in 1995.
Sales fell to A$352.5 million in 1996 from A$374.3 million and pre-tax earnings fell to A$18.1 million from A$23.5 million.
"The company is planning to benefit from both the improvement in demand and the significant restructuring implemented in the past two years," chairman Brian Healey said.
